ghost.e: The h in the spelling appears in the Prologue to William Caxton’s Royal Book, printed in 1484, in a reference to the “Holy Ghoost”. It was likely influenced by Middle Dutch gheest, a common variant of geest. Both Caxton and his assistant Wynkyn de Worde had connections to the Low Countries. The adjective and verb are derived from the noun.
ghost.g: A disembodied soul; a soul or spirit of a deceased person; a spirit appearing after death.
